Commentary on Surah al-Layl (The Night)

It is Meccan.

The Prophet (ﷺ) had earlier said to Mu'adh: "Why did you not pray with (the surahs) 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High' (87), 'By the sun and its brightness' (91), and 'By the night when it covers' (92)?"

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah: that he came to Syria, entered the Mosque of Damascus, prayed two rak'ahs in it, and said: "O Allah, grant me a righteous companion." He said: So he sat with Abu al-Darda', and Abu al-Darda' said to him: "Where are you from?" He said: "From the people of Kufa." He said: "How did you hear Ibn Umm 'Abd (Ibn Mas'ud) recite: ﴿By the night when it covers, and the day when it reveals itself﴾?" Alqamah said: "And the male and the female." Abu al-Darda' said: "I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as well, but these people kept on until they made me doubt." Then he said: "Was there not among you the keeper of the cushion (Ibn Mas'ud), and the confidant of the secret whom no one else knows (Hudhayfah), and the one who was protected from Satan by the tongue of the Prophet (ﷺ)?" [[Al-Musnad (6/449); the completion of the hadith is: "The keeper of the cushion: Ibn Mas'ud; the confidant of the secret: Hudhayfah; and the one protected from Satan: 'Ammar."]]

Al-Bukhari and Muslim also narrated it here, by way of al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: The companions of 'Abd Allah came to Abu al-Darda', and he sought them out and found them, and said: "Which of you recites to me the recitation of 'Abd Allah?" They said: "All of us." He said: "Which of you memorises best?" They pointed to Alqamah. He said: "How did you hear him recite: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾?" He said: "And the male and the female." He said: "I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite it this way, but these people want me to recite: ﴿And He who created the male and the female﴾. By Allah, I will not follow them." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4944) and Sahih Muslim no. (824).]]

This is the wording of al-Bukhari: Thus did Ibn Mas'ud recite it, and Abu al-Darda' (and Abu al-Darda' raised it to the Prophet ﷺ). As for the majority, they recited it as it is fixed in the Mushaf of the Imam 'Uthman throughout all the regions: ﴿And He who created the male and the female﴾.

So Allah swore by ﴿the night when it covers﴾, i.e., when it covers creation with its darkness, ﴿and the day when it reveals itself﴾, i.e., with its light and brightness, ﴿and He who created the male and the female﴾, like His saying: ﴿And We created you in pairs﴾ [An-Naba: 8], and His saying: ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 49].

Since the oath was by these contrary things, the thing sworn to is also contrary; therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾, i.e., the deeds of the servants that they earn are also contrary and different, so one does good and another does evil.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah﴾, i.e., gives what he is commanded to give, and fears Allah regarding his affairs, ﴿and believes in the best reward﴾, i.e., in the recompense for that. This was said by Qatadah; Khusayf said: "with the reward." Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Abu Salih and Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿and believes in the best reward﴾, i.e., in the replacement. Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami and al-Dahhak said: ﴿and believes in the best﴾, i.e., "There is no god but Allah." In a narration from 'Ikrimah: ﴿and believes in the best﴾, i.e., in what Allah has bestowed upon him. In a narration from Zayd ibn Aslam: ﴿and believes in the best﴾, he said: the prayer, the zakah, and the fasting; and at another time he said: and the charity of breaking the fast.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Safwan ibn Salih al-Dimashqi narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Zuhayr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, one who heard Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi narrating from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about "the best," and he said: "The best is Paradise." [[Narrated also by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15/69), ed. al-Ma'arif, by way of 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah from Zuhayr with the same chain.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So We will ease him toward ease﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: meaning toward good. Zayd ibn Aslam said: meaning toward Paradise.

Some of the early scholars said: "Among the reward of a good deed is the good deed after it, and among the punishment for an evil deed is the evil deed after it." Therefore He the Exalted said: ﴿But as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient﴾, i.e., withholds what he has, ﴿and considers himself self-sufficient﴾. 'Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: i.e., he was stingy with his wealth and considered himself independent of his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

﴿And denies the best﴾, i.e., the recompense in the Hereafter.

﴿So We will ease him toward hardship﴾, i.e., toward the path of evil, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights away, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [Al-An'am: 110]. The verses on this meaning are many, indicating that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, rewards whoever intends good with success in it, and whoever intends evil with abandonment, and all of that is by a predetermined decree. The hadiths indicating this meaning are many:

The narration of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him: Imam Ahmad said: 'Ali ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, al-'Attaf ibn Khalid narrated to me, a man from the people of Basrah narrated to me, from Talhah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, from his father, who said: I heard my father mention that his father heard Abu Bakr say: I said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "O Messenger of Allah, shall we act upon what has been finished, or upon a matter newly begun?" He said: "Rather, upon a matter that has already been finished." He said: "Then what is the point of action, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Each is made easy for what he was created for." [[Al-Musnad (1/5).]]

The narration of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: al-Bukhari said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the Baqi' al-Gharqad at a funeral, and he said: "There is not one of you whose place has not been written, in Paradise or in the Fire." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not then rely (on that)?" He said: "Act, for each is made easy for what he was created for." Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best, We will ease him toward ease﴾ up to His saying: ﴿toward hardship﴾. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4945).]]

It was also narrated by him by way of Shu'bah and Waki', from al-A'mash, similarly. [[Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (4946, 4947).]] Then he narrated it from 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, from Jarir, from Mansur, from Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him: We were at a funeral at Baqi' al-Gharqad, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and sat, and we sat around him. He had a staff, and he lowered his head and began to scratch the ground with his staff. Then he said: "There is not one of you—or: no soul that is breathed—except that its place has been written, in Paradise or in the Fire, and it has been written whether it is wretched or blessed." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not rely (on that) and leave action? Whoever among us is of the people of happiness will surely go to the people of happiness, and whoever among us is of the people of wretchedness will surely go to the people of wretchedness?" He said: "As for the people of happiness, they will be made easy for the deeds of the people of happiness, and as for the people of wretchedness, they will be made easy for the deeds of the people of wretchedness." Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best, We will ease him toward ease﴾, the verse. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4948).]]

It was also narrated by the rest of the compilers, through several routes, from Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah, with the same. [[Sahih Muslim no. (2647); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4694); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3344); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11678); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (78).]]

The narration of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn 'Ubayd Allah, who said: I heard Salim ibn 'Abd Allah narrating from Ibn 'Umar, who said: 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about what we do? Is it about a matter already finished, or a newly begun or innovated one?" He said: "About what has already been finished. So act, O son of al-Khattab, for each one is made easy (for his destiny). As for the one who is of the people of happiness, he acts for happiness, and as for the one who is of the people of wretchedness, he acts for wretchedness."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in (the book of) al-Qadar, from Bundar, from Ibn Mahdi, similarly, and said: "Hasan sahih." [[Al-Musnad (2/52); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2135).]]

Another hadith, from the narration of Jabir: Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we act for a matter already finished, or for a matter we are about to begin?" He said: "For a matter already finished." Suraqah said: "Then what is the point of action?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every worker is made easy for his work."

Muslim narrated it from Abu al-Tahir, from Ibn Wahb, similarly. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/144); Sahih Muslim no. (2648). Note: Suraqah is not mentioned in the narration of al-Tabari nor in the narration of Abu al-Tahir in Sahih Muslim; it occurs in Sahih Muslim by another route.]]

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Talq ibn Habib, from Bashir ibn Ka'b al-'Adawi, who said: Two young men asked the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we act upon what the pens have dried up with and what the decrees have run with, or upon something yet to be begun?" He said: "Rather, upon what the pens have dried up with and the decrees have run with." They said: "Then what is the point of action?" He said: "Act, for each worker is made easy for the work for which he was created." They said: "Then now we will strive and act." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/144).]]

The narration of Abu al-Darda': Imam Ahmad said: Haytham ibn Kharijah narrated to us, Abu al-Rabi' Sulayman ibn 'Utbah al-Sulami narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Maysarah ibn Halbas, from Abu Idris, from Abu al-Darda', who said: They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about what we do: is it a matter already finished, or something we are yet to begin?" He said: "Rather, a matter already finished." They said: "Then how is the action, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Every person is prepared for what he was created for." [[Al-Musnad (6/441).]]

Ahmad alone narrated it by this route.

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: al-Hasan ibn Salamah ibn Abi Kabshah narrated to me, 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr narrated to us, 'Abbad ibn Rashid narrated to us, from Qatadah, Khulayd al-'Asri narrated to me, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no day on which its sun sets except that on its two sides are two angels calling out with a voice that all of Allah's creation hears except the two weighty ones (humans and jinn): 'O Allah, give the one who spends a replacement, and give the one who withholds destruction.'" And Allah revealed in this regard in the Qur'an: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best, We will ease him toward ease. But as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best, We will ease him toward hardship﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/142).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from Ibn Abi Kabshah, with its chain similarly.

Another narration: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abd Allah al-Tihrani narrated to me, Hafs ibn Umar al-Adani narrated to us, al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that a man had a palm tree, and one of his palm trees had a branch extending over the house of a righteous, poor man who had dependents. When the man came and entered his house and took the dates from his palm tree, a date would fall and the poor man's children would take it. So the owner would descend from his palm tree and snatch the date from their hands, and if one of them put a date in his mouth, he would put his finger into the boy's throat and pull the date out of his throat. The poor man complained of this to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of what he was suffering from the owner of the palm tree. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Go." Then the Prophet ﷺ met the owner of the palm tree and said to him: "Give me your palm tree whose branch is over the house of so-and-so, and you will have a palm tree in Paradise in return for it." He said: "You have given [a promise], but it pleases me to have its dates, and I have many palm trees, and there is not one among them whose dates please me more than those." The Prophet ﷺ left, and a man who had been listening to the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and of the owner of the palm tree followed him. The man said: "O Messenger of Allah, if I take the palm tree and it becomes mine, and I then give it [to you], will you give me in exchange for it a palm tree in Paradise, as you gave him?" He said: "Yes." Then the man met the owner of the palm tree, and both of them had palm trees, and he said to him: "I inform you that Muhammad [has] given me a palm tree in Paradise in exchange for your leaning palm tree in the house of so-and-so. I said to him: 'You have given [a promise], but it pleases me to have its dates.'" The man fell silent, and he [the man who followed] said to him: "Do you think that if you sold it...?" He said: "No, unless I am given something for it, and I do not think I will be given [enough]." He said: "And what is your offer for it?" He said: "Forty palm trees." The man said: "You have come with a great matter! Your palm tree, you seek forty palm trees for it?!" Then they both fell silent, and he began another speech, then said: "I will give you forty palm trees." He said: "Bear witness for me if you are truthful." So he ordered some people and summoned them and said: "Bear witness that I have given him forty palm trees from my palms in exchange for his palm tree whose branch is in the house of so-and-so, son of so-and-so." Then he said: "What do you say?" The owner of the palm tree said: "I am content." Then he said afterwards: "There is no sale between me and you until we part." He said to him: "Allah has cancelled it for you, and I am not foolish when I gave you forty palm trees for your leaning palm tree." The owner of the palm tree said: "I am content, on condition that you give me the forty as I wish." He said: "You give them to me on a stalk." Then he waited a while, then said: "They are yours on a stalk," and he called witnesses for him and counted out forty palm trees on a stalk for him. Then they parted. The man went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the leaning palm tree in the house of so-and-so has become mine, so it is yours." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to the man who owned the house and said to him: "The palm tree is yours and for your dependents." Ikrimah said: Ibn Abbas said: then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾ up to His words: ﴿As for him who gives and fears [Allah], and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. But as for him who is miserly and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward difficulty﴾ to the end of the surah [[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/532), who said: "Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it with a weak chain from Ibn Abbas."]].

Thus did Ibn Abi Hatim narrate it, and it is a very strange hadith.

Ibn Jarir said: It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him: Harun ibn Idris al-Asamm narrated to me, Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, from Amir ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: Abu Bakr used to free [slaves] for [their acceptance of] Islam in Makkah. He would free old women and women when they embraced Islam. His father said to him: "My son, I see you freeing weak people. Why not free strong men who would stand with you, protect you and defend you?" He said: "O my father, I only want [what is with Allah]" (I think he said). He said: "Some of my family told me that this verse was revealed concerning him: ﴿As for him who gives and fears [Allah], and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease﴾" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/142).]].

And His words: ﴿And his wealth will not avail him when he falls [into the Fire]﴾. Mujahid said: that is, when he dies. Abu Salih and Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, said: "when he falls [into the Fire]."

Another narration: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abd Allah al-Tihrani narrated to me, Hafs ibn Umar al-Adani narrated to us, al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that a man had a palm tree, and one of his palm trees had a branch extending over the house of a righteous, poor man who had dependents. The poor man complained of this to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of what he was suffering from the owner of the palm tree. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Go." He said: "You have given [a promise], but it pleases me to have its dates, and I have many palm trees, and there is not one among them whose dates please me more than those." The Prophet ﷺ left, and a man who had been listening to the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and of the owner of the palm tree followed him. The man said: "O Messenger of Allah, if I take the palm tree and it becomes mine, and I then give it [to you], will you give me in exchange for it a palm tree in Paradise, as you gave him?" Commentary on Surah al-Layl (The Night)

It is Meccan.

The Prophet (ﷺ) had earlier said to Mu'adh: "Why did you not pray with (the surahs) 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High' (87), 'By the sun and its brightness' (91), and 'By the night when it covers' (92)?"

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah: that he came to Syria, entered the Mosque of Damascus, prayed two rak'ahs in it, and said: "O Allah, grant me a righteous companion." He said: So he sat with Abu al-Darda', and Abu al-Darda' said to him: "Where are you from?" He said: "From the people of Kufa." He said: "How did you hear Ibn Umm 'Abd (Ibn Mas'ud) recite: ﴿By the night when it covers, and the day when it reveals itself﴾?" Alqamah said: "And the male and the female." Abu al-Darda' said: "I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as well, but these people kept on until they made me doubt." Then he said: "Was there not among you the keeper of the cushion (Ibn Mas'ud), and the confidant of the secret whom no one else knows (Hudhayfah), and the one who was protected from Satan by the tongue of the Prophet (ﷺ)?" [[Al-Musnad (6/449); the completion of the hadith is: "The keeper of the cushion: Ibn Mas'ud; the confidant of the secret: Hudhayfah; and the one protected from Satan: 'Ammar."]]

Al-Bukhari and Muslim also narrated it here, by way of al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: The companions of 'Abd Allah came to Abu al-Darda', and he sought them out and found them, and said: "Which of you recites to me the recitation of 'Abd Allah?" They said: "All of us." He said: "Which of you memorises best?" They pointed to Alqamah. He said: "How did you hear him recite: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾?" He said: "And the male and the female." He said: "I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite it this way, but these people want me to recite: ﴿And He who created the male and the female﴾. By Allah, I will not follow them." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4944) and Sahih Muslim no. (824).]]

This is the wording of al-Bukhari: Thus did Ibn Mas'ud recite it, and Abu al-Darda' (and Abu al-Darda' raised it to the Prophet ﷺ). As for the majority, they recited it as it is fixed in the Mushaf of the Imam 'Uthman throughout all the regions: ﴿And He who created the male and the female﴾.

So Allah swore by ﴿the night when it covers﴾, i.e., when it covers creation with its darkness, ﴿and the day when it reveals itself﴾, i.e., with its light and brightness, ﴿and He who created the male and the female﴾, like His saying: ﴿And We created you in pairs﴾ [An-Naba: 8], and His saying: ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 49].

Since the oath was by these contrary things, the thing sworn to is also contrary; therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾, i.e., the deeds of the servants that they earn are also contrary and different, so one does good and another does evil.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah﴾, i.e., gives what he is commanded to give, and fears Allah regarding his affairs, ﴿and believes in the best reward﴾, i.e., in the recompense for that. This was said by Qatadah; Khusayf said: "with the reward." Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Abu Salih and Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿and believes in the best reward﴾, i.e., in the replacement. Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami and al-Dahhak said: ﴿and believes in the best﴾, i.e., "There is no god but Allah." In a narration from 'Ikrimah: ﴿and believes in the best﴾, i.e., in what Allah has bestowed upon him. In a narration from Zayd ibn Aslam: ﴿and believes in the best﴾, he said: the prayer, the zakah, and the fasting; and at another time he said: and the charity of breaking the fast.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Safwan ibn Salih al-Dimashqi narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Zuhayr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, one who heard Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi narrating from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about "the best," and he said: "The best is Paradise." [[Narrated also by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15/69), ed. al-Ma'arif, by way of 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah from Zuhayr with the same chain.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So We will ease him toward ease﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: meaning toward good. Zayd ibn Aslam said: meaning toward Paradise.

Some of the early scholars said: "Among the reward of a good deed is the good deed after it, and among the punishment for an evil deed is the evil deed after it." Therefore He the Exalted said: ﴿But as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient﴾, i.e., withholds what he has, ﴿and considers himself self-sufficient﴾. 'Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: i.e., he was stingy with his wealth and considered himself independent of his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

﴿And denies the best﴾, i.e., the recompense in the Hereafter.

﴿So We will ease him toward hardship﴾, i.e., toward the path of evil, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights away, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [Al-An'am: 110]. The verses on this meaning are many, indicating that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, rewards whoever intends good with success in it, and whoever intends evil with abandonment, and all of that is by a predetermined decree. The hadiths indicating this meaning are many:

The narration of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him: Imam Ahmad said: 'Ali ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, al-'Attaf ibn Khalid narrated to me, a man from the people of Basrah narrated to me, from Talhah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, from his father, who said: I heard my father mention that his father heard Abu Bakr say: I said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "O Messenger of Allah, shall we act upon what has been finished, or upon a matter newly begun?" He said: "Rather, upon a matter that has already been finished." He said: "Then what is the point of action, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Each is made easy for what he was created for." [[Al-Musnad (1/5).]]

The narration of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: al-Bukhari said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the Baqi' al-Gharqad at a funeral, and he said: "There is not one of you whose place has not been written, in Paradise or in the Fire." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not then rely (on that)?" He said: "Act, for each is made easy for what he was created for." Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best, We will ease him toward ease﴾ up to His saying: ﴿toward hardship﴾. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4945).]]

He said: "Some of my family told me that this verse was revealed concerning him: ﴿As for him who gives and fears [Allah], and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease﴾" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/142).]].

Commentary on Surah al-Layl (The Night)

It is Meccan.

The Prophet (ﷺ) had earlier said to Mu'adh: "Why did you not pray with (the surahs) 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High' (87), 'By the sun and its brightness' (91), and 'By the night when it covers' (92)?"

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah: that he came to Syria, entered the Mosque of Damascus, prayed two rak'ahs in it, and said: "O Allah, grant me a righteous companion." He said: So he sat with Abu al-Darda', and Abu al-Darda' said to him: "Where are you from?" He said: "From the people of Kufa." He said: "How did you hear Ibn Umm 'Abd (Ibn Mas'ud) recite: ﴿By the night when it covers, and the day when it reveals itself﴾?" Alqamah said: "And the male and the female." Abu al-Darda' said: "I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as well, but these people kept on until they made me doubt." Then he said: "Was there not among you the keeper of the cushion (Ibn Mas'ud), and the confidant of the secret whom no one else knows (Hudhayfah), and the one who was protected from Satan by the tongue of the Prophet (ﷺ)?" [[Al-Musnad (6/449); the completion of the hadith is: "The keeper of the cushion: Ibn Mas'ud; the confidant of the secret: Hudhayfah; and the one protected from Satan: 'Ammar."]]

Al-Bukhari and Muslim also narrated it here, by way of al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: The companions of 'Abd Allah came to Abu al-Darda', and he sought them out and found them, and said: "Which of you recites to me the recitation of 'Abd Allah?" They said: "All of us." He said: "Which of you memorises best?" They pointed to Alqamah. He said: "How did you hear him recite: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾?" He said: "And the male and the female." He said: "I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite it this way, but these people want me to recite: ﴿And He who created the male and the female﴾. By Allah, I will not follow them." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4944) and Sahih Muslim no. (824).]]

This is the wording of al-Bukhari: Thus did Ibn Mas'ud recite it, and Abu al-Darda' (and Abu al-Darda' raised it to the Prophet ﷺ). As for the majority, they recited it as it is fixed in the Mushaf of the Imam 'Uthman throughout all the regions: ﴿And He who created the male and the female﴾.

So Allah swore by ﴿the night when it covers﴾, i.e., when it covers creation with its darkness, ﴿and the day when it reveals itself﴾, i.e., with its light and brightness, ﴿and He who created the male and the female﴾, like His saying: ﴿And We created you in pairs﴾ [An-Naba: 8], and His saying: ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 49].

Since the oath was by these contrary things, the thing sworn to is also contrary; therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾, i.e., the deeds of the servants that they earn are also contrary and different, so one does good and another does evil.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah﴾, i.e., gives what he is commanded to give, and fears Allah regarding his affairs, ﴿and believes in the best reward﴾, i.e., in the recompense for that. This was said by Qatadah; Khusayf said: "with the reward." Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Abu Salih and Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿and believes in the best reward﴾, i.e., in the replacement. Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami and al-Dahhak said: ﴿and believes in the best﴾, i.e., "There is no god but Allah." In a narration from 'Ikrimah: ﴿and believes in the best﴾, i.e., in what Allah has bestowed upon him. In a narration from Zayd ibn Aslam: ﴿and believes in the best﴾, he said: the prayer, the zakah, and the fasting; and at another time he said: and the charity of breaking the fast.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Safwan ibn Salih al-Dimashqi narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Zuhayr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, one who heard Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi narrating from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about "the best," and he said: "The best is Paradise." [[Narrated also by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15/69), ed. al-Ma'arif, by way of 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah from Zuhayr with the same chain.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So We will ease him toward ease﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: meaning toward good. Zayd ibn Aslam said: meaning toward Paradise.

'Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: i.e., he was stingy with his wealth and considered himself independent of his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

﴿And denies the best﴾, i.e., the recompense in the Hereafter.

﴿So We will ease him toward hardship﴾, i.e., toward the path of evil, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights away, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [Al-An'am: 110]. He said: "Rather, upon a matter that has already been finished." He said: "Then what is the point of action, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Each is made easy for what he was created for." [[Al-Musnad (1/5).]]

The narration of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: al-Bukhari said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the Baqi' al-Gharqad at a funeral, and he said: "There is not one of you whose place has not been written, in Paradise or in the Fire." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not then rely (on that)?" He said: "Act, for each is made easy for what he was created for." Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best, We will ease him toward ease﴾ up to His saying: ﴿toward hardship﴾. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4945).]]

It was also narrated by him by way of Shu'bah and Waki', from al-A'mash, similarly. [[Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (4946, 4947).]] Then he narrated it from 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, from Jarir, from Mansur, from Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him: We were at a funeral at Baqi' al-Gharqad, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and sat, and we sat around him. He had a staff, and he lowered his head and began to scratch the ground with his staff. Then he said: "There is not one of you—or: no soul that is breathed—except that its place has been written, in Paradise or in the Fire, and it has been written whether it is wretched or blessed." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not rely (on that) and leave action? Whoever among us is of the people of happiness will surely go to the people of happiness, and whoever among us is of the people of wretchedness will surely go to the people of wretchedness?" He said: "As for the people of happiness, they will be made easy for the deeds of the people of happiness, and as for the people of wretchedness, they will be made easy for the deeds of the people of wretchedness." Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best, We will ease him toward ease﴾, the verse. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4948).]]

It was also narrated by the rest of the compilers, through several routes, from Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah, with the same. [[Sahih Muslim no. (2647); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4694); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3344); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11678); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (78).]]

The narration of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn 'Ubayd Allah, who said: I heard Salim ibn 'Abd Allah narrating from Ibn 'Umar, who said: 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about what we do? Is it about a matter already finished, or a newly begun or innovated one?" He said: "About what has already been finished. So act, O son of al-Khattab, for each one is made easy (for his destiny). As for the one who is of the people of happiness, he acts for happiness, and as for the one who is of the people of wretchedness, he acts for wretchedness."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in (the book of) al-Qadar, from Bundar, from Ibn Mahdi, similarly, and said: "Hasan sahih." [[Al-Musnad (2/52); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2135).]]

Another hadith, from the narration of Jabir: Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we act for a matter already finished, or for a matter we are about to begin?" He said: "For a matter already finished." Suraqah said: "Then what is the point of action?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every worker is made easy for his work."

Muslim narrated it from Abu al-Tahir, from Ibn Wahb, similarly. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/144); Sahih Muslim no. (2648). Note: Suraqah is not mentioned in the narration of al-Tabari nor in the narration of Abu al-Tahir in Sahih Muslim; it occurs in Sahih Muslim by another route.]]

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Talq ibn Habib, from Bashir ibn Ka'b al-'Adawi, who said: Two young men asked the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we act upon what the pens have dried up with and what the decrees have run with, or upon something yet to be begun?" He said: "Rather, upon what the pens have dried up with and the decrees have run with." They said: "Then what is the point of action?" He said: "Act, for each worker is made easy for the work for which he was created." They said: "Then now we will strive and act." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/144).]]

He said: "Rather, a matter already finished." They said: "Then how is the action, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Every person is prepared for what he was created for." [[Al-Musnad (6/441).]]

Ahmad alone narrated it by this route.

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: al-Hasan ibn Salamah ibn Abi Kabshah narrated to me, 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr narrated to us, 'Abbad ibn Rashid narrated to us, from Qatadah, Khulayd al-'Asri narrated to me, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no day on which its sun sets except that on its two sides are two angels calling out with a voice that all of Allah's creation hears except the two weighty ones (humans and jinn): 'O Allah, give the one who spends a replacement, and give the one who withholds destruction.'" And Allah revealed in this regard in the Qur'an: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best, We will ease him toward ease. But as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best, We will ease him toward hardship﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/142).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from Ibn Abi Kabshah, with its chain similarly.

Another narration: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abd Allah al-Tihrani narrated to me, Hafs ibn Umar al-Adani narrated to us, al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that a man had a palm tree, and one of his palm trees had a branch extending over the house of a righteous, poor man who had dependents. When the man came and entered his house and took the dates from his palm tree, a date would fall and the poor man's children would take it. So the owner would descend from his palm tree and snatch the date from their hands, and if one of them put a date in his mouth, he would put his finger into the boy's throat and pull the date out of his throat. The poor man complained of this to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of what he was suffering from the owner of the palm tree. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Go." Then the Prophet ﷺ met the owner of the palm tree and said to him: "Give me your palm tree whose branch is over the house of so-and-so, and you will have a palm tree in Paradise in return for it." He said: "You have given [a promise], but it pleases me to have its dates, and I have many palm trees, and there is not one among them whose dates please me more than those." The Prophet ﷺ left, and a man who had been listening to the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and of the owner of the palm tree followed him. The man said: "O Messenger of Allah, if I take the palm tree and it becomes mine, and I then give it [to you], will you give me in exchange for it a palm tree in Paradise, as you gave him?" He said: "Yes." Then the man met the owner of the palm tree, and both of them had palm trees, and he said to him: "I inform you that Muhammad [has] given me a palm tree in Paradise in exchange for your leaning palm tree in the house of so-and-so. I said to him: 'You have given [a promise], but it pleases me to have its dates.'" The man fell silent, and he [the man who followed] said to him: "Do you think that if you sold it...?" He said: "No, unless I am given something for it, and I do not think I will be given [enough]." He said: "And what is your offer for it?" He said: "Forty palm trees." The man said: "You have come with a great matter! Your palm tree, you seek forty palm trees for it?!" Then they both fell silent, and he began another speech, then said: "I will give you forty palm trees." He said: "Bear witness for me if you are truthful." So he ordered some people and summoned them and said: "Bear witness that I have given him forty palm trees from my palms in exchange for his palm tree whose branch is in the house of so-and-so, son of so-and-so." Then he said: "What do you say?" The owner of the palm tree said: "I am content." Then he said afterwards: "There is no sale between me and you until we part." He said to him: "Allah has cancelled it for you, and I am not foolish when I gave you forty palm trees for your leaning palm tree." The owner of the palm tree said: "I am content, on condition that you give me the forty as I wish." He said: "You give them to me on a stalk." Then he waited a while, then said: "They are yours on a stalk," and he called witnesses for him and counted out forty palm trees on a stalk for him. Then they parted. The man went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the leaning palm tree in the house of so-and-so has become mine, so it is yours." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to the man who owned the house and said to him: "The palm tree is yours and for your dependents." Thus did Ibn Abi Hatim narrate it, and it is a very strange hadith.

Ibn Jarir said: It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him: Harun ibn Idris al-Asamm narrated to me, Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, from Amir ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: Abu Bakr used to free [slaves] for [their acceptance of] Islam in Makkah. Another narration: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abd Allah al-Tihrani narrated to me, Hafs ibn Umar al-Adani narrated to us, al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that a man had a palm tree, and one of his palm trees had a branch extending over the house of a righteous, poor man who had dependents. When the man came and entered his house and took the dates from his palm tree, a date would fall and the poor man's children would take it. So the owner would descend from his palm tree and snatch the date from their hands, and if one of them put a date in his mouth, he would put his finger into the boy's throat and pull the date out of his throat. The poor man complained of this to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of what he was suffering from the owner of the palm tree. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Go." Then the Prophet ﷺ met the owner of the palm tree and said to him: "Give me your palm tree whose branch is over the house of so-and-so, and you will have a palm tree in Paradise in return for it." He said: "You have given [a promise], but it pleases me to have its dates, and I have many palm trees, and there is not one among them whose dates please me more than those." The Prophet ﷺ left, and a man who had been listening to the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and of the owner of the palm tree followed him. The man said: "O Messenger of Allah, if I take the palm tree and it becomes mine, and I then give it [to you], will you give me in exchange for it a palm tree in Paradise, as you gave him?" He said: "Yes." Then the man met the owner of the palm tree, and both of them had palm trees, and he said to him: "I inform you that Muhammad [has] given me a palm tree in Paradise in exchange for your leaning palm tree in the house of so-and-so. The man said: "You have come with a great matter! Your palm tree, you seek forty palm trees for it?!" Then they both fell silent, and he began another speech, then said: "I will give you forty palm trees." He said: "Bear witness for me if you are truthful." So he ordered some people and summoned them and said: "Bear witness that I have given him forty palm trees from my palms in exchange for his palm tree whose branch is in the house of so-and-so, son of so-and-so." Then he said: "What do you say?" The owner of the palm tree said: "I am content." Then he said afterwards: "There is no sale between me and you until we part." He said to him: "Allah has cancelled it for you, and I am not foolish when I gave you forty palm trees for your leaning palm tree." The owner of the palm tree said: "I am content, on condition that you give me the forty as I wish." He said: "You give them to me on a stalk." Then he waited a while, then said: "They are yours on a stalk," and he called witnesses for him and counted out forty palm trees on a stalk for him. Then they parted. Commentary on Surah al-Layl (The Night)

It is Meccan.

The Prophet (ﷺ) had earlier said to Mu'adh: "Why did you not pray with (the surahs) 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High' (87), 'By the sun and its brightness' (91), and 'By the night when it covers' (92)?"

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah: that he came to Syria, entered the Mosque of Damascus, prayed two rak'ahs in it, and said: "O Allah, grant me a righteous companion." He said: So he sat with Abu al-Darda', and Abu al-Darda' said to him: "Where are you from?" He said: "From the people of Kufa." He said: "How did you hear Ibn Umm 'Abd (Ibn Mas'ud) recite: ﴿By the night when it covers, and the day when it reveals itself﴾?" Alqamah said: "And the male and the female." Abu al-Darda' said: "I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as well, but these people kept on until they made me doubt." Then he said: "Was there not among you the keeper of the cushion (Ibn Mas'ud), and the confidant of the secret whom no one else knows (Hudhayfah), and the one who was protected from Satan by the tongue of the Prophet (ﷺ)?" [[Al-Musnad (6/449); the completion of the hadith is: "The keeper of the cushion: Ibn Mas'ud; the confidant of the secret: Hudhayfah; and the one protected from Satan: 'Ammar."]]

Al-Bukhari and Muslim also narrated it here, by way of al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: The companions of 'Abd Allah came to Abu al-Darda', and he sought them out and found them, and said: "Which of you recites to me the recitation of 'Abd Allah?" They said: "All of us." He said: "Which of you memorises best?" They pointed to Alqamah. He said: "How did you hear him recite: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾?" He said: "And the male and the female." He said: "I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite it this way, but these people want me to recite: ﴿And He who created the male and the female﴾. By Allah, I will not follow them." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4944) and Sahih Muslim no. (824).]]

This is the wording of al-Bukhari: Thus did Ibn Mas'ud recite it, and Abu al-Darda' (and Abu al-Darda' raised it to the Prophet ﷺ). As for the majority, they recited it as it is fixed in the Mushaf of the Imam 'Uthman throughout all the regions: ﴿And He who created the male and the female﴾.

So Allah swore by ﴿the night when it covers﴾, i.e., when it covers creation with its darkness, ﴿and the day when it reveals itself﴾, i.e., with its light and brightness, ﴿and He who created the male and the female﴾, like His saying: ﴿And We created you in pairs﴾ [An-Naba: 8], and His saying: ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 49].

Since the oath was by these contrary things, the thing sworn to is also contrary; therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾, i.e., the deeds of the servants that they earn are also contrary and different, so one does good and another does evil.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah﴾, i.e., gives what he is commanded to give, and fears Allah regarding his affairs, ﴿and believes in the best reward﴾, i.e., in the recompense for that. This was said by Qatadah; Khusayf said: "with the reward." Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Abu Salih and Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿and believes in the best reward﴾, i.e., in the replacement. Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami and al-Dahhak said: ﴿and believes in the best﴾, i.e., "There is no god but Allah." In a narration from 'Ikrimah: ﴿and believes in the best﴾, i.e., in what Allah has bestowed upon him. In a narration from Zayd ibn Aslam: ﴿and believes in the best﴾, he said: the prayer, the zakah, and the fasting; and at another time he said: and the charity of breaking the fast.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Safwan ibn Salih al-Dimashqi narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Zuhayr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, one who heard Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi narrating from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about "the best," and he said: "The best is Paradise." [[Narrated also by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15/69), ed. al-Ma'arif, by way of 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah from Zuhayr with the same chain.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So We will ease him toward ease﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: meaning toward good. Zayd ibn Aslam said: meaning toward Paradise.

Some of the early scholars said: "Among the reward of a good deed is the good deed after it, and among the punishment for an evil deed is the evil deed after it." Therefore He the Exalted said: ﴿But as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient﴾, i.e., withholds what he has, ﴿and considers himself self-sufficient﴾. 'Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: i.e., he was stingy with his wealth and considered himself independent of his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

﴿And denies the best﴾, i.e., the recompense in the Hereafter.

﴿So We will ease him toward hardship﴾, i.e., toward the path of evil, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights away, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [Al-An'am: 110]. The verses on this meaning are many, indicating that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, rewards whoever intends good with success in it, and whoever intends evil with abandonment, and all of that is by a predetermined decree. The hadiths indicating this meaning are many:

The narration of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him: Imam Ahmad said: 'Ali ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, al-'Attaf ibn Khalid narrated to me, a man from the people of Basrah narrated to me, from Talhah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, from his father, who said: I heard my father mention that his father heard Abu Bakr say: I said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "O Messenger of Allah, shall we act upon what has been finished, or upon a matter newly begun?" He said: "Rather, upon a matter that has already been finished." He said: "Then what is the point of action, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Each is made easy for what he was created for." [[Al-Musnad (1/5).]]

The narration of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: al-Bukhari said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the Baqi' al-Gharqad at a funeral, and he said: "There is not one of you whose place has not been written, in Paradise or in the Fire." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not then rely (on that)?" He said: "Act, for each is made easy for what he was created for." Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best, We will ease him toward ease﴾ up to His saying: ﴿toward hardship﴾. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4945).]]

It was also narrated by him by way of Shu'bah and Waki', from al-A'mash, similarly. [[Sahih al-Bukhari nos. In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah: that he came to Syria, entered the Mosque of Damascus, prayed two rak'ahs in it, and said: "O Allah, grant me a righteous companion." He said: "I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite it this way, but these people want me to recite: ﴿And He who created the male and the female﴾. [[Al-Musnad (1/5).]]

Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best, We will ease him toward ease﴾ up to His saying: ﴿toward hardship﴾. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4945).]]

Then he said: "There is not one of you—or: no soul that is breathed—except that its place has been written, in Paradise or in the Fire, and it has been written whether it is wretched or blessed." Ahmad alone narrated it by this route.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from Ibn Abi Kabshah, with its chain similarly.

Another narration: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abd Allah al-Tihrani narrated to me, Hafs ibn Umar al-Adani narrated to us, al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that a man had a palm tree, and one of his palm trees had a branch extending over the house of a righteous, poor man who had dependents. When the man came and entered his house and took the dates from his palm tree, a date would fall and the poor man's children would take it. So the owner would descend from his palm tree and snatch the date from their hands, and if one of them put a date in his mouth, he would put his finger into the boy's throat and pull the date out of his throat. The poor man complained of this to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of what he was suffering from the owner of the palm tree. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Go." Then the Prophet ﷺ met the owner of the palm tree and said to him: "Give me your palm tree whose branch is over the house of so-and-so, and you will have a palm tree in Paradise in return for it." He said: "You have given [a promise], but it pleases me to have its dates, and I have many palm trees, and there is not one among them whose dates please me more than those." The Prophet ﷺ left, and a man who had been listening to the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and of the owner of the palm tree followed him. The man said: "O Messenger of Allah, if I take the palm tree and it becomes mine, and I then give it [to you], will you give me in exchange for it a palm tree in Paradise, as you gave him?" He said: "Yes." Then the man met the owner of the palm tree, and both of them had palm trees, and he said to him: "I inform you that Muhammad [has] given me a palm tree in Paradise in exchange for your leaning palm tree in the house of so-and-so. The man said: "You have come with a great matter! Your palm tree, you seek forty palm trees for it?!" Then they both fell silent, and he began another speech, then said: "I will give you forty palm trees." He said: "Bear witness for me if you are truthful." So he ordered some people and summoned them and said: "Bear witness that I have given him forty palm trees from my palms in exchange for his palm tree whose branch is in the house of so-and-so, son of so-and-so." Commentary on Surah al-Layl (The Night)

It is Meccan.

The Prophet (ﷺ) had earlier said to Mu'adh: "Why did you not pray with (the surahs) 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High' (87), 'By the sun and its brightness' (91), and 'By the night when it covers' (92)?"

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah: that he came to Syria, entered the Mosque of Damascus, prayed two rak'ahs in it, and said: "O Allah, grant me a righteous companion." He said: So he sat with Abu al-Darda', and Abu al-Darda' said to him: "Where are you from?" He said: "From the people of Kufa." He said: "How did you hear Ibn Umm 'Abd (Ibn Mas'ud) recite: ﴿By the night when it covers, and the day when it reveals itself﴾?" Alqamah said: "And the male and the female." Abu al-Darda' said: "I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as well, but these people kept on until they made me doubt." Then he said: "Was there not among you the keeper of the cushion (Ibn Mas'ud), and the confidant of the secret whom no one else knows (Hudhayfah), and the one who was protected from Satan by the tongue of the Prophet (ﷺ)?" [[Al-Musnad (6/449); the completion of the hadith is: "The keeper of the cushion: Ibn Mas'ud; the confidant of the secret: Hudhayfah; and the one protected from Satan: 'Ammar."]]

Al-Bukhari and Muslim also narrated it here, by way of al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: The companions of 'Abd Allah came to Abu al-Darda', and he sought them out and found them, and said: "Which of you recites to me the recitation of 'Abd Allah?" They said: "All of us." He said: "Which of you memorises best?" They pointed to Alqamah. He said: "How did you hear him recite: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾?" He said: "And the male and the female." He said: "I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite it this way, but these people want me to recite: ﴿And He who created the male and the female﴾. By Allah, I will not follow them." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4944) and Sahih Muslim no. (824).]]

This is the wording of al-Bukhari: Thus did Ibn Mas'ud recite it, and Abu al-Darda' (and Abu al-Darda' raised it to the Prophet ﷺ). As for the majority, they recited it as it is fixed in the Mushaf of the Imam 'Uthman throughout all the regions: ﴿And He who created the male and the female﴾.

So Allah swore by ﴿the night when it covers﴾, i.e., when it covers creation with its darkness, ﴿and the day when it reveals itself﴾, i.e., with its light and brightness, ﴿and He who created the male and the female﴾, like His saying: ﴿And We created you in pairs﴾ [An-Naba: 8], and His saying: ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 49].

Since the oath was by these contrary things, the thing sworn to is also contrary; therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾, i.e., the deeds of the servants that they earn are also contrary and different, so one does good and another does evil.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah﴾, i.e., gives what he is commanded to give, and fears Allah regarding his affairs, ﴿and believes in the best reward﴾, i.e., in the recompense for that. This was said by Qatadah; Khusayf said: "with the reward." Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Abu Salih and Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿and believes in the best reward﴾, i.e., in the replacement. Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami and al-Dahhak said: ﴿and believes in the best﴾, i.e., "There is no god but Allah." In a narration from 'Ikrimah: ﴿and believes in the best﴾, i.e., in what Allah has bestowed upon him. In a narration from Zayd ibn Aslam: ﴿and believes in the best﴾, he said: the prayer, the zakah, and the fasting; and at another time he said: and the charity of breaking the fast.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Safwan ibn Salih al-Dimashqi narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Zuhayr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, one who heard Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi narrating from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about "the best," and he said: "The best is Paradise." [[Narrated also by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15/69), ed. al-Ma'arif, by way of 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah from Zuhayr with the same chain.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So We will ease him toward ease﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: meaning toward good. Zayd ibn Aslam said: meaning toward Paradise.

Some of the early scholars said: "Among the reward of a good deed is the good deed after it, and among the punishment for an evil deed is the evil deed after it." Therefore He the Exalted said: ﴿But as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient﴾, i.e., withholds what he has, ﴿and considers himself self-sufficient﴾. 'Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: i.e., he was stingy with his wealth and considered himself independent of his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

﴿And denies the best﴾, i.e., the recompense in the Hereafter.

﴿So We will ease him toward hardship﴾, i.e., toward the path of evil, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights away, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [Al-An'am: 110]. It is Meccan.

The Prophet (ﷺ) had earlier said to Mu'adh: "Why did you not pray with (the surahs) 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High' (87), 'By the sun and its brightness' (91), and 'By the night when it covers' (92)?"

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah: that he came to Syria, entered the Mosque of Damascus, prayed two rak'ahs in it, and said: "O Allah, grant me a righteous companion." He said: So he sat with Abu al-Darda', and Abu al-Darda' said to him: "Where are you from?" He said: "From the people of Kufa." Abu al-Darda' said: "I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as well, but these people kept on until they made me doubt." Then he said: "Was there not among you the keeper of the cushion (Ibn Mas'ud), and the confidant of the secret whom no one else knows (Hudhayfah), and the one who was protected from Satan by the tongue of the Prophet (ﷺ)?" They said: "All of us." He said: "Which of you memorises best?" They pointed to Alqamah. He said: "How did you hear him recite: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾?" He said: "And the male and the female." He said: "I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite it this way, but these people want me to recite: ﴿And He who created the male and the female﴾. By Allah, I will not follow them." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4944) and Sahih Muslim no. (824).]]

This is the wording of al-Bukhari: Thus did Ibn Mas'ud recite it, and Abu al-Darda' (and Abu al-Darda' raised it to the Prophet ﷺ). As for the majority, they recited it as it is fixed in the Mushaf of the Imam 'Uthman throughout all the regions: ﴿And He who created the male and the female﴾.

So Allah swore by ﴿the night when it covers﴾, i.e., when it covers creation with its darkness, ﴿and the day when it reveals itself﴾, i.e., with its light and brightness, ﴿and He who created the male and the female﴾, like His saying: ﴿And We created you in pairs﴾ [An-Naba: 8], and His saying: ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 49].

Since the oath was by these contrary things, the thing sworn to is also contrary; therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾, i.e., the deeds of the servants that they earn are also contrary and different, so one does good and another does evil.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah﴾, i.e., gives what he is commanded to give, and fears Allah regarding his affairs, ﴿and believes in the best reward﴾, i.e., in the recompense for that. This was said by Qatadah; Khusayf said: "with the reward." Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Abu Salih and Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿and believes in the best reward﴾, i.e., in the replacement. Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami and al-Dahhak said: ﴿and believes in the best﴾, i.e., "There is no god but Allah." In a narration from 'Ikrimah: ﴿and believes in the best﴾, i.e., in what Allah has bestowed upon him. In a narration from Zayd ibn Aslam: ﴿and believes in the best﴾, he said: the prayer, the zakah, and the fasting; and at another time he said: and the charity of breaking the fast.

He said: "Rather, upon a matter that has already been finished." He said: "Then what is the point of action, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Each is made easy for what he was created for." [[Al-Musnad (1/5).]]

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not then rely (on that)?" He said: "Act, for each is made easy for what he was created for." Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best, We will ease him toward ease﴾ up to His saying: ﴿toward hardship﴾. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4945).]]

He had a staff, and he lowered his head and began to scratch the ground with his staff. Then he said: "There is not one of you—or: no soul that is breathed—except that its place has been written, in Paradise or in the Fire, and it has been written whether it is wretched or blessed." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not rely (on that) and leave action? Whoever among us is of the people of happiness will surely go to the people of happiness, and whoever among us is of the people of wretchedness will surely go to the people of wretchedness?" He said: "As for the people of happiness, they will be made easy for the deeds of the people of happiness, and as for the people of wretchedness, they will be made easy for the deeds of the people of wretchedness." He said: "Rather, upon what the pens have dried up with and the decrees have run with." They said: "Then what is the point of action?" Ahmad alone narrated it by this route.

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not then rely (on that)?" He said: "Act, for each is made easy for what he was created for." Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best, We will ease him toward ease﴾ up to His saying: ﴿toward hardship﴾. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4945).]]

When the man came and entered his house and took the dates from his palm tree, a date would fall and the poor man's children would take it. So the owner would descend from his palm tree and snatch the date from their hands, and if one of them put a date in his mouth, he would put his finger into the boy's throat and pull the date out of his throat. The poor man complained of this to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of what he was suffering from the owner of the palm tree. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Go." Then the Prophet ﷺ met the owner of the palm tree and said to him: "Give me your palm tree whose branch is over the house of so-and-so, and you will have a palm tree in Paradise in return for it." He said: "You have given [a promise], but it pleases me to have its dates, and I have many palm trees, and there is not one among them whose dates please me more than those." The Prophet ﷺ left, and a man who had been listening to the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and of the owner of the palm tree followed him. The man said: "O Messenger of Allah, if I take the palm tree and it becomes mine, and I then give it [to you], will you give me in exchange for it a palm tree in Paradise, as you gave him?" He said: "Yes." Then the man met the owner of the palm tree, and both of them had palm trees, and he said to him: "I inform you that Muhammad [has] given me a palm tree in Paradise in exchange for your leaning palm tree in the house of so-and-so. I said to him: 'You have given [a promise], but it pleases me to have its dates.'" The man fell silent, and he [the man who followed] said to him: "Do you think that if you sold it...?" He said: "No, unless I am given something for it, and I do not think I will be given [enough]." He said: "And what is your offer for it?" He said: "Forty palm trees." The man said: "You have come with a great matter! Your palm tree, you seek forty palm trees for it?!" Then they both fell silent, and he began another speech, then said: "I will give you forty palm trees." He said: "Bear witness for me if you are truthful." So he ordered some people and summoned them and said: "Bear witness that I have given him forty palm trees from my palms in exchange for his palm tree whose branch is in the house of so-and-so, son of so-and-so." Then he said: "What do you say?" The owner of the palm tree said: "I am content." Then he said afterwards: "There is no sale between me and you until we part." He said to him: "Allah has cancelled it for you, and I am not foolish when I gave you forty palm trees for your leaning palm tree." The owner of the palm tree said: "I am content, on condition that you give me the forty as I wish." He said: "You give them to me on a stalk." Then he waited a while, then said: "They are yours on a stalk," and he called witnesses for him and counted out forty palm trees on a stalk for him. Then they parted. The man went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the leaning palm tree in the house of so-and-so has become mine, so it is yours." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to the man who owned the house and said to him: "The palm tree is yours and for your dependents." Why not free strong men who would stand with you, protect you and defend you?" He said: "O my father, I only want [what is with Allah]" (I think he said). He said: "Some of my family told me that this verse was revealed concerning him: ﴿As for him who gives and fears [Allah], and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease﴾" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/142).]].

And His words: ﴿And his wealth will not avail him when he falls [into the Fire]﴾. Mujahid said: that is, when he dies. Abu Salih and Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, said: "when he falls [into the Fire]."

Qatadah said: ﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance﴾, meaning: We make clear what is lawful and what is unlawful. Others said: Whoever takes the path of guidance reaches Allah. He compared this to His saying: ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾ [An-Nahl: 9]. This was related by Ibn Jarir.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first life﴾, meaning: all of it is Our dominion, and I am the one who disposes of both.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So I have warned you of a Fire that blazes﴾, Mujahid said: meaning, it flares up.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, who said: I heard al-Nu'man ibn Bashir delivering a sermon, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivering a sermon, saying: "I warn you of the Fire, I warn you of the Fire, I warn you of the Fire, to the extent that a man in the marketplace would hear it from this place of mine." He said: "Until a cloak that was on his shoulder fell down at his feet."

Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq narrated to me: I heard al-Nu'man ibn Bashir delivering a sermon and saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed, the least punished of the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection is a man upon whose soles two embers are placed, from which his brain boils."

Al-Bukhari related it.

Muslim said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the least punished of the people of the Fire is one who has two sandals and two straps of fire, from which his brain boils like a cauldron. * *

Al-Bukhari related it from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Fulayh, with the same wording.

* *

﴿And for no one has he any favor [due] to be repaid﴾, meaning: his giving is not a repayment to one who has done him a kindness, so that he gives in return for that. Rather, he gives it only ﴿seeking the countenance of his Lord, the Most High﴾, meaning: hoping that he will attain the sight of Him in the Hereafter in the gardens of the Paradises. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And he is going to be satisfied﴾, meaning: and he who is characterized by these attributes will surely be satisfied.

Many of the exegetes mentioned that these verses were revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, to the extent that some related a consensus of the exegetes on that. There is no doubt that he is included in them, and most worthy of their general application, since their wording is general, namely the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And the most righteous will be kept away from it, who gives his wealth to purify himself, and for no one has he any favor [due] to be repaid﴾. Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, there is no harm for one who is called from there, but will anyone be called from all of them?" He said: "Yes, and I hope you will be among them."
